claims.text: Step-by-step decision planning achieves a higher F1 score in smart home action generation compared to all-at-once action generation.
Consistently selecting the action with the maximum estimated point-wise dependency yields higher mean precision than random action selection during step-by-step planning.
Increasing the decision threshold for estimated point-wise dependency increases the mean precision of generated actions.
Increasing the decision threshold for estimated point-wise dependency decreases the mean recall of generated actions.
Point-wise dependency neural estimation quantifies uncertainty for black-box LLMs in a single inference without requiring access to token output logits.

evidence.description: Step-by-step planning achieved F1 scores of 0.152 (random selection) and 0.164 (maximum selection), outperforming all-at-once generation which scored an F1 of 0.140 at a point-wise dependency threshold of 1.0.
In step-by-step planning at a 1.0 threshold, selecting the maximum point-wise dependency action achieved a mean precision of 0.134 compared to 0.126 for random action selection.
For maximum step-by-step planning, increasing threshold t from 0.0 to 1.0 to 1.627 raised mean precision from 0.123 to 0.134 to 0.139.
For maximum step-by-step planning, increasing threshold t from 0.0 to 1.0 to 1.627 reduced mean recall from 0.232 to 0.212 to 0.209.

The auxiliary neural network estimates pointwise dependency r_theta(a, x') using representations from Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1 with GRU and linear layers via relative predictive coding optimization without reading token logits.

methodologies.name: Point-wise Dependency Neural Estimation with Conformal Prediction
methodologies.description: An auxiliary neural network trained via relative predictive coding estimates pointwise dependencies between prompt-history and action pairs to filter actions using thresholds derived from conformal prediction.
datasets: Synthetic Smart Home Dataset (20k prompt-action pairs)

limitations.text: White-box uncertainty quantification methods require access to token logits, internal layer outputs, or model parameters.
Existing black-box uncertainty quantification methods require generating multiple responses per input, making them computationally demanding.
The evaluation relies on a strict exact match criterion between generated and ground-truth actions, which fails to account for semantic similarity.
Neural network approximation in density-ratio fitting inevitably produces negative estimated point-wise dependency values for some inputs.

future_work.text: Conducting a human study where actions are selected step-by-step by human users to evaluate decision planning strategies.
Extending evaluation methodologies to include semantic similarity measures alongside exact match criteria.
